items.title: Paul Barbarin Interview, 1959-12-23
items.q: I played a job with Chris Kelly on a court, it was a house party

ctx.x: I thought maybe you were in the 5th Precinct.

No, no, I don't see that 5th Precinct. Let me tell you about that 5th Precinct, or the first time with the 5th Precinct. It was either the first time, the second time. I went there twice. Off and up, you know. That's right, I played a job with Chris Kelly on a court, it was a house party on a court between Maraday and Manifel. And, well, the pay wasn't much, I think it was a dollar quarter, the pay was about a dollar quarter. It might have been a dollar. But the people was giving us quarters, a nickel, a dime,…
You know, I don't know. What happened? So they took me.

items.title: Paul Barbarin Interview, 1957-03-27
items.q: They said Chris Kelly had a lot of glow. All of his glow.

ctx.x: Big Ike? Yeah, Big Ike, yeah. That's him? Yeah. Just like Chris Kelly. They said Chris Kelly had a lot of glow. All of his glow. All of his glow. Always smart. He's always smart. Did he wear expensive clothes? Well, he's a pretty neat guy. Don't make me terrible.
Old drummers, that is the first drummers that inspired you. People like Red Happy you were talking about.

items.title: Paul Barbarin Interview, 1959-01-07
items.q: I recall one time I played a pick-need with him.

ctx.x: and I'm glad I'm muting. That's a point on the story.
That's a point on the story. That's a point on the story. That's a point on the story. I recall one time I played a pick-need with him.
